subject: ACME POC: Evaluation plan & methodology (offline vs online shadow)
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: John Dwyer <john.dwyer@acme.com>, Priya Singh <priya.singh@acme.com>
Cc: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>, Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 15 Jul 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: ACME POC: Evaluation plan & methodology (offline vs online shadow)

Thanks for the call this morning — great alignment overall. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we can get the POC kicked off next week. Attaching the initial evaluation plan and a spreadsheet with the suggested success criteria.

Recap / objectives:
- Goal: validate Redwood's inference runtime for ACME's customer-facing summarization and routing flows.
- Key success criteria (high level): accuracy on priority intents, latency under 300ms p50 for peak path, hallucination rate < 5%, and cost per 1k tokens within expected budget. Detailed metrics in attached XLSX.

Proposed POC structure (4 weeks):
1) Week 0 (prep): data access, anonymization checklist, and instrumenting shadow endpoints
2) Weeks 1-2 (online shadow): route 5-10% of live traffic to Redwood shadow (no return to prod) to capture live distribution; collect logs for online metrics
3) Weeks 3-4 (offline eval + sampling): run offline evals on sampled historical queries + hand-graded rubrics for edge cases

Evaluation methodology: we recommend a hybrid approach: online shadow for distributional validation + offline graded sampling to measure quality and hallucination. This balances realistic traffic coverage with deeper human-evaluated checks.

Proposed grading rubric (draft):
- Accuracy / relevance (40%)
- Latency / reliability (20%)
- Hallucination / factuality (20%)
- Cost / token efficiency (20%)

Ownership and next steps:
- Redwood: Marissa (sales lead / kickoff), Dylan (technical lead: shadow setup & instrumentation), Rachel (eval lead: rubric & grading pool)
- ACME: John (product), Priya (engineering), Sara (ops)

Please confirm these success criteria and the hybrid methodology. If OK, we'll schedule a 30-45 minute kickoff next Tue/Thu and finalize the instrumentation checklist.

Attachments: redwood-poc-eval-plan-v1.pdf, acme-success-criteria.xlsx

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com

Subject: Re: ACME POC: Evaluation plan & methodology (offline vs online shadow)

John — thanks, great questions. Short answers below and a few additional details.

1) Online shadow timeline: yes — plan is Week 1-2 online shadow (5-10% sample), Weeks 3-4 offline eval + hand grading. We can be flexible on sampling rate; we'll work with ACME eng to tune.

2) Data access & retention: Redwood will only ingest the minimal fields required for evaluation (payload redaction by default). For the POC we propose a 30-day retention window for raw logs (can be shortened on request). We support customer-managed keys (KMS/HSM) and will provide an export and deletion workflow at the end of the POC. I'll have legal/security share the standard evidence pack (SOC2 artifact summary) if that helps.

3) Sampling approach: stratified by intent and time window is recommended — we'll provide a sampling script. For hand grading we'll do a stratified random sample of ~300 queries across intents (adjustable).

Draft grading rubric (numbers / thresholds we propose):
- Accuracy / relevance (40%): weighted score; target >= 0.85 average on sampled queries
- Latency (20%): p50 < 300ms for primary path, p95 < 800ms
- Hallucination / factuality (20%): < 5% critical hallucinations on sampled set
- Cost efficiency (20%): cost per 1k tokens within the agreed budget (see attached XLSX for target)

Operational ask for kickoff:
- ACME: confirm point-of-contact for instrumentation (Priya), confirm data retention constraint
- Redwood: we'll provide the shadow endpoint + sampling script, Rachel will provide the grading template and instructions for raters

I'll update the attached plan with these thresholds and share a short kickoff agenda. Proposed kickoff slots: Tue 7/20 1:00-2:00pm PST or Thu 7/22 9:00-9:45am PST — which works for you?

Best,
Marissa
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Folks — looping you in with the ACME thread above. Quick internal alignment items before kickoff: 

1) Dylan: can you own the shadow endpoint + sampling script (deliverable: endpoint + runbook + retention config). We'll need a small instrumentation guide for Priya and her team. Aim: have endpoint ready by Mon 7/19 EOD.

2) Rachel: own the grading rubric, rater instructions, and the Google Sheet template. For hand grading plan: ~300 samples, stratified across intents. Also propose blind grading (raters don't see model/plugin labels) and an inter-rater agreement check on 10% of samples. Deliverable: rubric + sample sheet by Mon 7/19 EOD.

3) Metrics dashboard: can we wire a simple Looker/Sheets export with accuracy/hallucination counters? Optional but helpful for ACME's PM.

4) Risk / security notes: keep data redaction as default; support KMS for this POC. I'll follow up with Legal for the evidence pack for ACME's security team if they request it.

I'll be running the kickoff and will own the project timeline with ACME. Proposed internal prep sync: Mon 7/19 10:00am PST — 30 minutes to validate artifacts.

Thanks — Marissa

Thanks Marissa — I'll take the rubric & grading work. A few notes: 

- I'll prepare a blind grading template with columns for intent, expected answer (if available), model output, rater score (0-2), and freeform notes.
- Inter-rater reliability: we'll double-grade 10% of the sample set and compute Cohen's kappa; target kappa > 0.6.
- Proposed thresholds (draft): accuracy >= 85% on sampled set; critical hallucinations < 5%; mean rater score >= 1.5/2 for priority intents.
- For edge-case evaluation, I'll include a small set (~25) of high-risk queries that will be graded by two senior raters.

Dylan — I'll need the instrumented logs (anonymized) and a sample extractor script so I can pull the stratified sample. Can you confirm you'll have that by Mon 7/19?

Confirmed kickoff: Tue 7/20 1:00-1:45pm PST works for ACME per John's note. I'll share the grading template and instructions by EOD Mon 7/19.

Thanks — Rachel
